items.title: Sequential digital cognitive screening and plasma biomarkers for detection of Alzheimer’s disease
items.author: Craig E. L. Stark
items.content: Researchers tested a sequential triaging approach that combined digital cognitive assessments and blood tests for the detection of Alzheimer’s disease. They found these two tools could save more than 60% of individuals from detailed cognitive evaluations and up to 85% from needing amyloid brain scans.

items.title: Decoding the role of cellular senescence in wounds
items.author: Saranya P. Wyles
items.content: Studies that involve the direct manipulation of senescent cells, either by addition or elimination, in wound models have yielded conflicting results. This inconsistency probably reflects the inherently dynamic nature of wound healing and the complexity of targeting cellular senescence. In this Comment, we systematically evaluate current studies with respect to timing, experimental design and interventional strategies to clarify the role of various senescent-cell subpopulations in the wound healing process.

items.title: Age-related impairment of oncogenic surveillance promotes liver tumor initiation
items.author: Ming Xu
items.content: Using a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence in hepatocytes, Yan, Zhu and colleagues report that aging weakens senescence immunosurveillance, enabling liver tumors lacking the initiating oncogene mutation. Spp1+ macrophage depletion or senolytic treatment reduces tumor incidence in aged mice.

items.title: Comparing plasma p-tau217 and plasma p-tau217/Aβ<sub>42</sub> with CSF biomarkers for assessing Alzheimer’s disease pathology
items.author: Michael Weiner
items.content: Blood tests for Alzheimer’s disease, including regulatory authorized p-tau217 and p-tau217/AB42, are accessible and cost-effective diagnostic tools. This study shows that they perform similarly to authorized cerebrospinal fluid tests in detecting Alzheimer’s disease pathology in patients.

items.title: Aged natural killer cells get back into shape
items.author: Pamela L. Wenzel
items.content: Aging natural killer (NK) cells might retain their killing machinery yet struggle to deploy it. Liu and colleagues now link this defect to retinoid-associated lipid remodeling, and show that inhibiting fatty acyl chain elongation restores the mechanical features of NK cells that are essential for antitumor activity in preclinical models of human cancers.
